questions: What does “When you roll this die, each face appears.” mean – does each face have equal probability of appearing?
Are the numbers on a die’s faces guaranteed to be distinct, or can the same number appear on multiple faces of the same die?
When choosing two dice “optimally,” are we allowed to choose the same die twice (i.e., roll the same die two times) or must the two dice be distinct?
If the two chosen dice are distinct, does the order of selection matter for the probability calculation, or is the pair considered unordered?
How should the answer be formatted – as a floating‑point number, a reduced fraction, or with a specific precision (e.g., 10⁻⁶)?
If the optimal probability is zero (no pair can ever match), should we output “0”, “0.0”, or something else?
Are there any constraints on the magnitude of the output (e.g., should we avoid scientific notation) and is there a required error tolerance for floating‑point answers?
If multiple pairs of dice achieve the same maximal probability, does it matter which pair we consider, or is only the probability value required?
answers: Yes — each face is equally likely (probability 1/K_i) when the die is rolled.

inline_prompts:
There are N dice.  
The i-th die has K_i faces, with the numbers A_{i,1}, A_{i,2}, \ldots, A_{i,K_i} written on them.  
When you roll this die, each face appears. Yes — each face is equally likely (probability 1/K_i) when the die is rolled.  
You choose two dice from the N dice and roll them.  
Determine the probability that the two dice show the same number, when the dice are chosen optimally.  
Input  
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:  
N  
K_1 A_{1,1} A_{1,2} \dots A_{1,K_1}  
\vdots  
K_N A_{N,1} A_{N,2} \dots A_{N,K_N}  
Output  
Print the answer.  
Constraints  
- 2 \leq N \leq 100  
- 1 \leq K_i  
- K_1 + K_2 + \dots + K_N \leq 10^5  
- 1 \leq A_{i,j} \leq 10^5  
- All input values are integers.
